about.nostrasia: Started in 2023, it's a place where people who build Nostr, use it, or are just curious about it come together. Past editions featured talks and LTs, hands-on sessions, a market, the Nostr Shrine and more. The 2024 and 2025 editions were held in Tokyo.
about.nostr: A protocol for decentralized social media that doesn't depend on any particular company. Instead of signing up with an email address, you make your own keys. Your public key (npub) is an ID you can share with others; your secret key (nsec) is something only you keep. Posts are stored on servers called relays, and you can read and write them with any app (client) you like. You can cheer on posts you like with a zap ⚡ (a way to send a small amount of bitcoin).

how.lead: Keys are circles, relays are squares. Four diagrams walk through how a Nostr post reaches its readers.

1.name: Keys
1.title: Make your keys
1.body: First, you make a pair of keys: a secret key <c>nsec</c> and a public key <c>npub</c>. Your npub is the ID that identifies you, and it's fine to share. Your nsec is the secret key only you hold. You don't need to sign up with an email address or anything else.

2.name: Signature
2.title: Sign
2.body: When you write a post, you sign it with your secret key. Thanks to the signature, anyone can check that you really wrote it, wherever it ends up.

3.name: Relays ×3
3.title: Send it to relays
3.body: You send the signed post to several relays. A relay is a server that stores posts and passes them along. Even if one goes down, the same post stays on the others.

4.name: App
4.title: Read it in an app
4.body: An app (client) gathers posts from whichever relays you like and shows them. As long as you have your keys, you keep the same account even if you switch apps. You can also send a zap ⚡ to posts you like.

keys.a: npub is your public key — like a business card, it's fine to share. nsec is your secret key — like a password, only you should keep it. Unlike a password, it can't be reissued if you lose it.
